overall_reason: The header, phone menu button and comparison table come from a finished kit with declared hover, focus-visible and disabled rules, but the first screen carries two differently filled buttons for one action and the tool directory gives every card its own full-width filled 'View details' button.

score.reason: T-PRIMARY-COUNT fails on the hero and the tool directory (CMP-004), T-TABLE-READ finds left-aligned prices, and T-STATE-MATRIX, T-WHERE-AM-I and T-PHONE-NAV pass as far as the capture reaches; the stack-builder flow was not captured.

visitor_mode: Persuade, with an Operate tail (a goal picker that starts a three-question stack builder). No 00-contract.md: inferred from the hero 'Tell us the goal. We'll build the stack.' and the goal-card grid.

findings.title: One primary action per view
findings.where: header 'Build my stack' and hero 'Find my stack →', 1440, tiles/1440-00.png
findings.evidence: The components table lists two filled variants on the first screen: 'Build my stack' in oklch(0.198 0.021 268) near-black and 'Find my stack →' in oklch(0.549 0.238 264.6) blue, both pill-shaped (radius 33554400). The nav also carries a 'Find My Stack' text link. Three labels point the visitor to the same builder.
findings.before: Two filled buttons in two colours, 'Build my stack' and 'Find my stack', plus a nav link 'Find My Stack', all for one action.
findings.after: One label for the builder, word for word, in the header and hero (CMP-121); the header copy as a quieter outlined or text button so the blue hero button is the one filled primary.
findings.why: A visitor sees two loud buttons with different names and cannot tell they are the same action.
findings.root: button variant used site-wide for the header CTA

findings.title: One filled primary per view (a dialog counts as its own page)
findings.where: AI Tools Directory cards, 1440, tiles/1440-01.png and tiles/1440-02.png
findings.evidence: Six tool cards each end in a full-width near-black filled 'View details' button (the 8-count dark variant, heights 36px). On tile 1440-02 six filled buttons sit on one screen, each as heavy as the header CTA.
findings.before: Every directory card carries a full-width filled 'View details' button.
findings.after: The whole card as the link with the tool name as its heading, or a text link 'View details' per card, so the filled style stays for the builder.
findings.why: Six identical filled buttons on one screen erase the difference between the page's main action and a routine detail link.

findings.title: Text left, numbers right with tabular figures, actions right
findings.evidence: The table row reads five columns (TOOL, CATEGORY, PRICE, LEVEL, BEST FOR) with prices '$20/mo', '$15/mo', '$5/mo' set left-aligned under a left-aligned head. The table's numeric alignment record is empty.
findings.before: Prices left-aligned in a proportional column.
findings.after: PRICE right-aligned with tabular figures, its head right-aligned to match.
findings.why: Visitors compare prices down the column; left-aligned figures of different widths do not line up.

findings.title: No popups, newsletter modals, chat bubbles, help pills
findings.where: fixed 'Edit with Lovable' pill, bottom right, 1440 and 375, fold-1440.png and fold-375.png
findings.evidence: A fixed dark pill 'Edit with Lovable' with a close button sits over the bottom-right corner at both widths; at 375 it covers the start of the next section. The capture clicked its 'Dismiss' button (overlay trigger t2) and recorded it as a complementary region 'Edit with Lovable'.
findings.before: A builder-platform badge floats over content on every screen.
findings.after: Remove the platform badge from the published site.
findings.why: The pill covers content the visitor did not ask to be covered and advertises the tool, not the product.

findings.title: On a phone keep the naming and action columns in view
findings.evidence: The table row records width_px 560 and wider_than_screen true at 375 inside an overflow-x-auto wrapper, so the BEST FOR column sits off-screen behind a horizontal scroll.
findings.before: A 560px table scrolls sideways inside a 375 screen.
findings.after: Each tool as a labelled block at 375 (name, then price, level and best-for as label and value lines).
findings.why: A phone visitor has to scroll sideways to read the column that says what each tool is for.

strengths: The stylesheet declares hover (41 rules), focus-visible (11), disabled (14) and expanded or open (23) states, and the focus_ring sweep found no invisible focus stops, only one stop covered by the sticky header.
The 375 header keeps the logo, the USD/INR switch and a named 'Open menu' button (36x36), so the top destinations stay one tap away.
The USD/INR switch marks the selected currency with a filled pill (tiles/1440-00.png), a clear selected state.
The ten goal cards are each one whole-card link with a category label, a head and one line, with no extra button inside.
not_investigated: The stack-builder flow ('Find my stack') beyond the home page: the async capture found no primary action, so its loading, failure and step states were not seen.
What the phone menu holds and how it opens and closes: the capture opens triggers at 1440 only.
Inline validation and error placement: the page has no fields.
Focus moving into an overlay and back, scroll lock and backdrop click: nothing that opened was a dialog.
Keyboard operation of custom widgets: lens-a11y.
T-FIELD-READ, T-ERROR-PATH and T-FIRST-RUN: no fields, no failure run and no onboarding on the captured page.
1 cross-origin stylesheet could not be read; declared-state counts cover the 119 readable rules only.
